items.title: Section: The Ten Purity Precepts Open — From a Genuinely Pure Motive to a Precisely Balanced Mind

items.zh: 云何菩薩清淨戒？當知此戒略有十種。一者、初善受戒。唯為沙門三菩提故，非為命故。二者、不太沈戒。於違犯時，遠離微薄生悔愧故；及不太舉戒，遠離非處生悔愧故。三者、離懈怠戒。於睡眠樂、倚樂、臥樂不耽著故，晝夜勤修諸善品故。四者、離諸放逸所攝受戒。修習如前所說五支不放逸故。五者、正願戒。遠離利養恭敬貪故，不願生天，而自要期修梵行故。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's purity precept? One should know this precept is, in brief, of ten kinds. First, the precept of a genuinely good initial reception — taken up purely for the sake of the renunciant path and supreme awakening, never merely to secure a livelihood. Second, the precept free of excessive withdrawal — steering clear of only a faint, insufficient regret at an actual violation; together with the precept free of excessive agitation — steering clear of feeling regret and shame in situations where none is actually warranted. Third, the precept free of laziness — not indulging the pleasure of sleep, of reclining, or of lying down, but diligently cultivating every wholesome practice day and night. Fourth, the precept encompassed by freedom from every kind of carelessness — cultivating the five-part diligence already described earlier. Fifth, the precept of properly ordered aspiration — free of any craving for gain or reverence, with no wish for heavenly rebirth, resolved instead purely on cultivating the genuinely pure conduct that leads to liberation.

items.title: Section: Five More Purity Precepts Close the Entire Nine-Category System — and the Śrāvaka Stage's Own Ten Marks of Impairment

items.zh: 六者、軌則具足所攝受戒。於諸威儀所作眾事善品加行妙善圓滿，如法身語正現行故。七者、淨命具足所攝受戒。離矯詐等一切邪命過失法故。八者、離二邊戒。遠離受用欲樂、自苦二邊法故。九者、永出離戒。遠離一切外道見故。十者、於先所受無損失戒。於先所受菩薩淨戒，無缺減故，無破壞故。如是十種，是名菩薩清淨戒。
items.en: Sixth, the precept encompassed by fully proper conduct — carrying out every posture, every daily task, and every wholesome practice with genuinely excellent and complete propriety, body and speech consistently manifesting exactly as the dharma prescribes. Seventh, the precept encompassed by a fully pure livelihood — free of deceptive posturing and every other fault of dishonest livelihood. Eighth, the precept free of both extremes — steering clear of both indulgence in sensory pleasure and self-punishing austerity. Ninth, the precept of genuine, lasting release — entirely free of every non-Buddhist view of a fixed self. Tenth, the precept of no loss with respect to what was already received — the bodhisattva precepts once properly received suffering no deficiency and no breakdown whatsoever. These ten together are called a bodhisattva's purity precept.

items.zh: 如是菩薩大尸羅藏，能起當來大菩提果。謂依此故，菩薩淨戒波羅蜜多得圓滿已，現證無上正等菩提。

items.title: Section: Five Lasting Benefits of Holding the Precepts — Dying Without Fear, Like Setting Down a Poisoned Cup

items.zh: 乃至未證無上菩提，依此無量菩薩戒藏正勤修習，常能獲得五種勝利。一者、常為十方諸佛護念。二者、將捨命時，住大歡喜。三者、身壞已後，在在所生，常與淨戒若等若增諸菩薩眾為其同分、為同法侶，為善知識。四者、成就無量大功德藏，能滿淨戒波羅蜜多。五者、現法後法常得成就自性淨戒，戒成其性。
items.en: Right up until supreme awakening is realised, relying on this immeasurable treasury of the bodhisattva precepts and diligently practising it brings five constant benefits. First, being constantly held in the protective awareness of the buddhas of the ten directions. Second, at the moment of death, abiding in great joy. Third, after this body has perished, wherever one is subsequently born, constantly finding oneself among bodhisattvas of equal or greater discipline, as genuine companions on the same path, comrades in the same practice, and true spiritual friends. Fourth, accomplishing an immeasurable, vast treasury of merit, thereby fulfilling the perfection of discipline. Fifth, in this present life and in every life to come, constantly coming to possess purity of discipline as one's own innate nature, discipline itself becoming one's very character.

items.title: Section: The Discipline Chapter Closes — Three Precepts, Three Tasks, One Complete System — and the Perfection of Patience Opens

items.zh: 如是如上所說一切自性戒等九種尸羅，當知三種淨戒所攝。謂律儀戒、攝善法戒、饒益有情戒。如是三種菩薩淨戒，以要言之，能為菩薩三所作事。謂律儀戒能安住其心，攝善法戒能成熟自佛法，饒益有情戒能成熟有情。如是總攝一切菩薩所應作事。所謂欲令現法樂住安住其心，身心無倦，成熟佛法、成熟有情。如是菩薩唯有爾所菩薩淨戒，唯有爾所淨戒勝利，唯有爾所淨戒所作。除此無有若過若增。過去菩薩求大菩提，已於中學；未來菩薩求大菩提，當於中學；普於十方無邊無際諸世界中現在菩薩求大菩提，今於中學。
items.en: All nine kinds of discipline described above — from intrinsic nature onward — should be understood as encompassed within three precepts: the precept of discipline, the precept of gathering wholesome dharmas, and the precept of benefiting sentient beings. In brief, these three bodhisattva precepts accomplish three tasks for a bodhisattva: the precept of discipline settles the mind; the precept of gathering wholesome dharmas matures one's own qualities as a buddha; and the precept of benefiting sentient beings matures other beings. In this way, every task a bodhisattva needs to accomplish is fully encompassed: dwelling in genuine ease in this present life with a settled mind, body and mind free of weariness, maturing one's own buddha-qualities, and maturing other beings. A bodhisattva's precepts are exactly this much, their benefits are exactly this much, and their function is exactly this much — there is nothing beyond this, and nothing to add to it. Bodhisattvas of the past who sought supreme awakening have already trained in exactly this; bodhisattvas of the future who seek supreme awakening will train in exactly this; and bodhisattvas presently existing throughout the boundless worlds of the ten directions who seek supreme awakening are training in exactly this even now. From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter eleven: patience.

items.title: Section: The Perfection of Patience Opens — the Same Ninefold Verse, Now Applied to Patience

items.zh: 云何菩薩忍波羅蜜多？嗢拕南曰：自性、一切、難、一切門、善士、一切種、遂求、二世樂、清淨，如是九種相，是名略說忍。謂九種相忍，名為菩薩忍波羅蜜多。一、自性忍，二、一切忍，三、難行忍，四、一切門忍，五、善士忍，六、一切種忍，七、遂求忍，八、此世他世樂忍，九、清淨忍。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's perfection of patience? A summary verse states: "Intrinsic nature, comprehensive scope, difficult practice; comprehensive gateways, virtuous persons; comprehensive kinds, fulfilling requests; both-worlds happiness, purity — these nine kinds of mark are, in brief, called patience." These nine marks of patience together constitute a bodhisattva's perfection of patience: first, the patience of intrinsic nature; second, comprehensive patience; third, the patience of difficult practice; fourth, comprehensive-gateway patience; fifth, virtuous-person patience; sixth, comprehensive-kind patience; seventh, fulfilling-requests patience; eighth, the patience of happiness in this world and the next; ninth, purity patience.

items.title: Section: The Intrinsic Nature of Patience — Three Classical Grades, from Simple Tolerance to Effortless Realisation

items.zh: 云何菩薩自性忍？謂諸菩薩或思擇力為所依止，或由自性堪忍怨害，遍於一切皆能堪忍、普於一切皆能堪忍。由無染心，純悲愍故，能有堪忍。當知此則略說菩薩忍之自性。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's patience of intrinsic nature? Bodhisattvas rely either on the power of deliberate reflection, or on an innate temperamental capacity to endure hostility and harm, and in either case remain pervasively tolerant of everything, and broadly able to endure everything. Because the mind is free of any defiling affliction, and moved purely by genuine compassion, they are able to remain patient. One should understand this as, in brief, a bodhisattva's patience of intrinsic nature.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive Patience Opens — Lay and Ordained, Each With Three Kinds

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切忍？當知此忍略有二種。一、依在家品忍，二、依出家品忍。當知依此二種品忍各有三種。一、耐他怨害忍，二、安受眾苦忍，三、法思勝解忍。云何菩薩耐他怨害忍？
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive patience? One should know this patience is, in brief, of two kinds: first, patience belonging to the lay category; second, patience belonging to the ordained category. One should know that each of these two categories has three further kinds: first, patience enduring others' hostility and harm; second, patience calmly bearing every kind of suffering; third, the patience of resolute understanding grounded in careful reflection on the dharma.

blocks.text: The ten marks of pure discipline, the benefits of keeping it, and the opening of the perfection of patience.

Discipline "taken up purely for the sake of the renunciant path and awakening, never merely to secure a livelihood"; neither too sunk (lax) nor too raised (anxious) (Master Cháng Bǎi: sinking is torpor, raising is restlessness; to keep recalling a confessed fault is itself a fault); free of heedlessness; with right aspiration; proper conduct; pure livelihood; free of the two extremes; free of all outside views (Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders may free themselves from desire but not from the three realms); and without loss.

"Constantly held in the protective awareness of the Buddhas"; "at the moment of death, abiding in great joy": Master Cháng Bǎi quotes, "joyful at life's end, like setting down a poisoned cup"; after death, born among bodhisattvas of the same precepts; a treasury of merit; and the perfection of discipline.

All nine aspects fall under the three storehouses: discipline settles the mind; gathering the good ripens one's own qualities; benefiting beings ripens others. Venerable Miào Jìng: "who would dare say this? Only Maitreya."
The same nine-part frame. Master Cháng Bǎi: from discipline comes patience.

Relying on reflection or innate capacity, bodhisattvas endure "because the mind is free of defiling affliction, and moved purely by compassion". Master Cháng Bǎi: one with nothing left to endure is truly patient.

For lay and ordained alike: enduring others' hostility; calmly bearing suffering; and the patience of resolute understanding of the Dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: patience towards beings, towards phenomena, towards the unborn.

quiz.q: The first purity precept, "a good initial reception" — what motive does the treatise require?
options: solely for the renunciant path and awakening, not to make a living
quiz.why: "Taken up purely for the sake of the renunciant path and awakening, never merely to secure a livelihood." Venerable Miào Jìng: one who completely cuts off greed, hatred, and delusion is a "śramaṇa." Master Cháng Bǎi: otherwise one becomes a "shaven-headed worldling," which must be avoided.

quiz.q: "Not too sunken" and "not too raised" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain these?
options: sinking is torpor, raising is restlessness; repeatedly recalling a fault after confession is excessive restlessness — the arrow of regret obstructs calm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: sinking means torpor; raising means restlessness. Confession brings ease; recalling the fault over and over afterwards is excessive restlessness — the arrow of regret in the heart obstructs calm abiding.

quiz.q: What is the ninth purity precept, "permanent emancipation"?
quiz.why: "Ninth, the precept of permanent emancipation — free of all non-Buddhist views." Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders may free themselves from desire and attain absorptions, even up to the peak of existence, yet not escape.

quiz.q: Among the five benefits of practising the bodhisattva precepts, what happens "at the moment of death"?
quiz.why: "First, being constantly held in the protective awareness of the buddhas of the ten directions. Second, at the moment of death, abiding in great joy." Master Cháng Bǎi: reflecting that in the next life one will meet buddhas and bodhisattvas, one transcends the fear of death and is greatly joyful.

quiz.q: What three tasks do the three pure precepts accomplish for a bodhisattva?
options: restraint settles the mind, gathering the good matures one's own buddha-qualities, benefiting beings matures beings
quiz.why: "The precept of discipline settles the mind; the precept of gathering wholesome dharmas matures one's own buddha-qualities; the precept of benefiting beings matures beings." Master Cháng Bǎi: restraint enables the bodhisattva to attain calm abiding and settle the mind.

quiz.q: On intrinsic patience, what does Master Cháng Bǎi say is true great patience?
options: one with nothing left to endure has true great patience; if something must still be endured, the patience is limited and may cause illness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one with nothing to endure is truly greatly patient; if there are still things to be endured, the patience has limits and will cause problems — that is false patience.

quiz.q: The two lectures focus differently on this section. What does each explain?
options: Cháng Bǎi maps the three to patience towards beings, towards dharmas, and towards non-arising; Miào Jìng explains lay as still living in the house of affliction, ordained as having left it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: enduring harm is also called patience towards beings; bearing suffering, patience towards dharmas; resolute understanding, acceptance of non-arising. Venerable Miào Jìng: the lay person still lives in the house of affliction; the ordained has left it and entered the saṅgha.
